highlights.title: Lock-screen widget redesign and font options
changes: You can now add and reorder lock-screen widgets using drag-and-drop instead of tap-to-add/remove.
The Detailed lock-screen layout gains a new double-width glucose widget that occupies two configuration slots.
The Simple lock-screen widget exposes font face and font size options and shows a preview in its configuration screen.
Font choices for the Simple widget are included in the Live Activity state so changes apply to the lock-screen activity.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1566: Expand Lock Screen Widget styles

highlights.title: Remote meal edit and delete commands
changes: Trio can accept remote delete_meal and edit_meal commands to remove or replace logged meals.
An edit operation deletes the old meal and recreates it, so the meal receives a new id.
Remote actions wait for Nightscout, Health and Tidepool updates and report Nightscout failures in the command ack.
Meals that include fat/protein but lack the shared fpuID are rejected for remote changes with a clear message.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1579: Add delete_meal and edit_meal remote commands
Add delete_meal and edit_meal remote commands

highlights.title: Improved Pod connections and Libre CGM info
changes: Trio can connect to InPlay pods in the background on iPhone 16 and 17e.
Trio gives up faster when a pod cannot be reached to avoid long hangs.
Trio stops sending pod state updates once pod deactivation starts.
Pod alert acknowledgments are saved earlier so they persist across sessions.
LibreLoop now records Libre 3 sensor events, tags backfilled readings, reports paired sensor model, and shows an in-app.

highlights.title: Glucose Bobble uses a black background
changes: Glucose Bobble contact images now always use a black background.
This prevents the bobble's white text from being hidden on watchOS.
Other contact images continue to use the background you selected.

includedPullRequests.title: Expand Lock Screen Widget styles
includedPullRequests.body: This PR includes a partial redesign of the Live Activity widget configuration system with drag-and-drop support, adds a new double-width glucose widget variant for the Detailed style, and enables font customization for the Simple Lock Screen layout. ## Key Changes ### Widget Configuration Redesign - **Drag-and-drop reordering**: Replaced the tap-to-add/remove system with an intuitive drag-and-drop interface where widgets can be dragged between the layout and a palette - **Ordered list model**: Changed from fixed four-slot array to an ordered list (`placedItems`) that's more intuitive for drag operations - **Visual feedback**: Added drop target highlighting and hover states to indicate where widgets will be placed - **Slot capacity system**: Implemented slot width tracking to support double-width widgets within the four-slot constraint https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ae72f36-4de6-44cb-a1c5-a085d40913ee ### New Double-Width Widget - Added `currentGlucoseWide` variant that displays glucose, trend arrow, and delta on a single line - Occupies two of the four configuration slots - Introduced `wideContinuation` placeholder item to track the second slot in the saved layout - Updated serialization to expand ordered layout into fixed slot array for Live Activity consumption ### Simple Layout Font Customization - Created new `LiveActivitySimpleWidgetConfiguration` view for Simple layout settings - Added `LiveActivityFontFace` enum (default, rounded, serif, monospaced) and `LiveActivityFontSize` enum (small, medium, large, extra large) - Integrated font settings into `TrioSettings` and `LiveActivityAttributes.SimpleViewStyle` - Added live preview showing how font choices affect the glucose reading display - Font sizes backed by Dynamic Type for proper scaling with system text size https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f2896cf-b2e9-4c4f-97ad-21615249e02b ### Implementation Details - Drag payload uses JSON `Transferable` representation for cross-app compatibility - Layout persistence converts between ordered list and fixed slot array formats - Drop validation prevents invalid states (gaps, repeats, overruns) - Accessibility labels updated for drag-drop interactions - Settings export includes new font configuration options - Live Activity extension updated to render the new wide widget variant and apply font styling

includedPullRequests.title: Add delete_meal and edit_meal remote commands
includedPullRequests.body:
Lets a follower app (LoopFollow) delete or replace a meal Trio has logged. Companion LoopFollow PR: https://github.com/loopandlearn/LoopFollow/pull/756.

Thanks to @aug0211 for #1417, which established the need and mapped out the areas involved. This takes the same idea with a smaller protocol.

## Protocol

Request (inside the existing encrypted payload):
- `command_type`: `delete_meal` or `edit_meal`
- `meal_id`: the Nightscout `id` of the meal root, or of any of its carb equivalents (their `id` is the root's `fpuID`). Trio resolves either to the root.
- `command_id`: echoed back in the ack
- `edit_meal` also carries `carbs`, `fat`, `protein`, `scheduled_time`; `delete_meal` must not.

Ack (existing return notification) gains `command_id`, `meal_id`, `result` (`deleted`, `updated`, `not_found`, `rejected`). For an edit, `meal_id` is the new root id.

## Principles

- Edit is delete + recreate, the same path the History editor uses. The meal gets a new id.
- A stale or replayed command finds no meal and is answered with `not_found`, so no extra bookkeeping is needed.
- Service deletes (Nightscout, Health, Tidepool) are awaited before the Core Data delete, and before the new meal is uploaded. Nightscout failures are reported in the ack text.
- A failed `determineBasalSync` after the change is logged, not treated as a command failure.
- Window: target meal and new time must be within 24 h back / 12 h ahead. `maxCarbs`/`maxFat`/`maxProtein` apply.
- Unknown `command_type` values are rejected with an ack instead of failing decoding silently.

## Changes

- `CarbEntryMutationService`: meal delete/replace orchestration moved out of `History.StateModel`; History and the remote handler share it.
- `CarbsStorage.fetchMealRoot(handle:)`; `saveCarbsToCoreData` keeps a UUID id supplied by the caller.
- Nightscout treatments now carry `fpuID` on the root and its carb equivalents.
- Nightscout profile gets `remoteCommands`, the list of command types this build accepts, so followers can hide unsupported actions.
- Roots with fat/protein but no `fpuID` (Shortcuts-created meals today) are rejected with a clear message; linking them is a separate follow-up.

## Known limitation

Meals imported from Nightscout have no Trio `id` in their Nightscout document. They are not offered for remote change by LoopFollow, and as today a local delete leaves the Nightscout copy.

## Tests

CarbsStorage, CarbEntryMutationService, ContainerResolution and RemoteMealMutationPayload suites. Verified in the simulator by injecting encrypted commands: delete by root id, delete by carb-equivalent id, edit, stale id, out-of-window, over-max, unknown command type, unlinked root.

includedPullRequests.title: Update Submodules, Fastlane and Browser Build Runner Images
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

Bumps OmnipodKit to the current tip of `dev`, updates fastlane to 2.240.1, and pins the
Ubuntu runners so the browser build stops emitting a notice annotation on every run. 

## OmnipodKit Updates

- **Connect on demand in the background for InPlay pods on iPhone 16/17e** (#190) — the follow-on
  to the eager-connect work, extending it to background connects.
- **Give up promptly when a pod cannot be reached** (#183) — avoids long hangs against an
  unreachable pod.
- **Stop reporting state to the delegate once deactivation has begun** (#186) — no more state
  updates racing a deactivation.
- **Persist a pod alert acknowledgment before the session runs** (#185).
- Minor cleanup and bulletproofing.

Touches `PeripheralManager`, `OmniPumpManager`, and the deactivate-pod and settings view models.

## LibreLoop Updates

`c6e9cc1` → `4d16e5d` (12 commits). Three things landed on `loopandlearn/LibreLoop`'s
`legacy-loopkit-compat` branch, which is now level with `LoopKit/LibreLoop@main`.

**Upstream sync**
- **Record Libre 3 sensor states and ends as CGM events** (LibreLoop#19)
- **Tag historical and clinical gap-fill readings as backfill** (LibreLoop#23)
- **Report the paired sensor's model and send status updates** (LibreLoop#24)
- **Add device manufacturer and picker subtitle** (LibreLoop#22)
- Compiler-warning cleanup (LibreLoop#21)

**In-app non-affiliation notice** (LibreLoop#25)

The README already said LibreLoop is not an Abbott product, which only reaches people who read the
README. It is now shown in the app too: a short form at the bottom of the apply-sensor setup
screen, and the full form as the last section of the CGM settings screen.


## Browser build: removing the recurring annotation

Every browser-build run currently finishes with a notice annotation:

> The `ubuntu-latest` label will migrate to Ubuntu 26 beginning October 19, 2026.

Pinning `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` → `ubuntu-26.04` removes it and makes the runner explicit before
the migration lands, rather than being moved silently. Applied to all seven occurrences across
`build_trio.yml`, `validate_secrets.yml`, `auto_version_dev.yml`, `add_to_project.yml` and
`stale_issues.yml`. LoopWorkspace did the same in `ef70ffb` ("use xcode-27 and ubuntu-26.04 for all
yml files"). Every workflow was re-parsed as YAML after the change.

### fastlane 2.236.1 → 2.240.1

Matches Loop v3.14.9, whose bump commit is titled *"update to fastlane 2.240.1, fixes security
warning for rubyzip"*. fastlane 2.236.1 resolves `rubyzip (>= 2.0.0, < 3.0.0)` → **2.4.1**, which
carries open advisories; 2.240.1 requires `rubyzip (>= 3.4.0, < 4.0.0)` → **3.7.0**.
